observation: SessionStore::create() generates a new active session directory whenever the preferred id already exists; it does not enforce one active session per task. WorkflowPlanCommand already rejects multiple active sessions, but WorkflowStartCommand previously called create() unconditionally. Retrying workflow start after a recall failure could therefore create a second active session and make later approve/close resolution ambiguous. WorkflowStartCommand now reuses the single active session and rejects an already-corrupt multi-active state before recall compilation.

evidence.reference: PR #28 CodeRabbit review thread PRRT_kwDOTALgUs6XZVxl: repeated workflow start can create multiple active sessions

evidence.summary: WorkflowStartCommand tests proved a retry reuses the existing active session and a pre-existing multi-active state fails before recall. PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, self-shape, and installed release-set dogfood were all green.

hypothesis: Every workflow entrypoint that creates or resumes session state must preserve the same one-active-session-per-task invariant; retries should reuse the active session rather than allocate a new one.
validated_conclusion: Workflow session orchestration has at most one active session per task. Start and plan may reuse the one active session; if more than one active session already exists, fail explicitly before doing further task work. A retry after partial failure must not create another active session.
